items.text: PROBLEM SOLVING

items.label: list_item
items.text: d The solubility of a substance is usually measured in units of g per 100g of water. The mass of 1 dm³ of water is 1000 g. Use the value that you obtained in c to calculate the solubility of strontium hydroxide as g of strontium hydroxide per 100 g of water. (A,: H = 1, O = 16, Sr = 88) (2)

items.label: list_item
items.text: e The calculation used in d gives only an approximate value for the solubility because the volume changes when a substance is dissolved in water. Describe an experiment that the student could carry out to determine a more accurate value for how much strontium hydroxide dissolves in 100g of water at this temperature. You can assume that you are given 50 cm³ of saturated strontium hydroxide solution. You should include a description of the apparatus you would use and the measurements you would make. (5)

items.label: text
items.text: A student carried out some experiments using dilute sulfuric acid.

items.label: list_item
items.text: a He found that 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide solution was neutralised by 20.0cm³ of the dilute sulfuric acid.

items.label: text
items.text: The equation for the reaction is

items.label: text
items.text: 2NaOH(aq) + H2SO₄(aq) → Na2SO₄(aq) + 2H2O(l)

items.label: text
items.text: Calculate the concentration of the sulfuric acid in mol/dm³. (4)

items.label: list_item
items.text: b 100 cm³ of this same sulfuric acid was reacted with magnesium.

items.label: formula
items.text: M g ( s ) + H _ { 2 } S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) \rightarrow M g S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) + H _ { 2 } ( g )

items.label: list_item
items.text: i Magnesium is a metal. Describe the structure and bonding in a piece of magnesium. (ε)

items.label: list_item
items.text: ii Magnesium is malleable. Explain in terms of structure and bonding why magnesium is malleable. (2)

items.label: list_item
items.text: iii Calculate the amount in moles of sulfuric acid that was used. (1)

items.label: list_item
items.text: iv The student used 0.100 g of magnesium in the experiment. Work out whether the sulfuric acid or the magnesium was in excess.

items.label: list_item
items.text: v Calculate the volume of hydrogen gas that would be produced at rtp in this experiment. (Assume that the molar volume at rtp of hydrogen is 24000 cm³.)

items.label: list_item
items.text: vi When the student did the experiment they collected 94 cm³ of gas. Calculate the percentage yield of the experiment.

items.label: list_item
items.text: c The student electrolysed the solution of magnesium sulfate.

items.label: list_item
items.text: i State the name of the product formed at the cathode. (1)

items.label: list_item
items.text: ii Oxygen gas is formed at the anode. Write an ionic half-equation for the formation of oxygen at the anode. (2)
